turns.speaker: Miss Havisham

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that he was to abandon his frivolous excuses and engage in a lively game with Estella, and that he was to begin immediately.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip explained that he didn't want to play games that might make Estella laugh at him, and that he was afraid of being ridiculed.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham insisted that Estella was not prone to laughter at the expense of others, and that Pip was to take that as a promise of her fair treatment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip explained that he was a poor boy from the village and didn't have the proper clothes to play games with Estella, and that he didn't want to make a spectacle of himself.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that he was a foolish boy to make excuses and that he would not be deterred from playing with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip explained that he was afraid of being a burden to Miss Havisham, and that he didn't want to take up her time with frivolous games.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes flashed with a mixture of expectation and annoyance as she instructed Pip to take Estella by the hand and accompany her to the drawing room, where games were waiting, with a stern warning to put aside any further excuses or hesitation.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was worried about making a mistake and getting things wrong, and that he didn't want to disappoint her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Estella to bring a new set of cards and a box of sweetmeats from the parlour, her eyes never leaving Pip's hesitant face as she spoke.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip asked if he might know what games they were going to play, and if it would be long, and if he might be in the way.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that he was squandering her time with his feeble excuses, and that it was his obligation to learn and obey the lessons assigned to him by Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he didn't know if he was supposed to play with Estella, and that he wasn't very good at games.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes narrowed as she spoke in a low, even tone, 'Pip, come closer, and do not fidget like a nervous child. You are here to learn and be instructed by Estella, not to indulge in frivolous questions.'
